title: Sell a home and buy a new one with a mortgage in the Solver
summary: Model a move in the Solver: sell the current home, buy the next one with a mortgage, and see the leftover cash and new costs in Cash Flow.

chapters.label: Mark and Laura plan to move to a new home when Mark retires.
On Techniques, add an Asset transaction for the year Mark retires.
Sell their Primary Home. Foundry fills in its value in 2033.
Their gain qualifies for the home-sale exclusion, so it isn't taxed.
Add the new home: a $1,100,000 house that grows 3% a year.
Enter its property tax in the year they buy it: $9,000.
The sale covers the $600,000 down payment, with $492,047 left over.
Save it. On Cash Flow, 2033 now shows the leftover money coming in.
Click 2033 for the details. The leftover arrives as Other Inflows.
The mortgage payment and the new property tax start the same year.
In the table, Other Expenses carry both costs every year after.

steps: **Add an asset transaction.** On the Solver's **Techniques** tab, select **Asset transaction**. Enter a **Name** and pick the **Year**. A milestone such as **Client Retirement** ties the move to that event.

**Sell the current home.** Select the sale under **Sell** and choose it in **Asset to Sell**. **Sale value** fills in with the home's projected value in that year. Tick **Qualifies for home-sale gain exclusion (§121)** when it applies.
**Add the new home.** Select **+ Add buy**, then enter its **Asset Name**, **Purchase Price**, **Growth Rate** and **Annual Property Tax**.

**Add the mortgage.** Open **Mortgage / Financing** and enter the **Amount**, **Rate** and **Term (mo)**. **Combined net** shows the proceeds minus the cash the purchase needs, and **Surplus goes to** picks where the rest lands. Select **Save**.

**See it on Cash Flow.** On the **Cash Flow** report, select the bar for the year of the move. The money left over shows under **Other Inflows**, and the mortgage payment and property tax under **Liabilities** and **Real Estate**.
**Check the later years.** Select **Expand table**. **Other Expenses** carries the mortgage payment and property tax in every year after the move.
goodToKnow: **Purchase Price** and **Annual Property Tax** are in the dollars of the year you buy, not today's.
Leave **Growth Rate** blank and the new home keeps the same value every year.
Without the §121 box, the whole gain on the sale is taxed in the year of the move.
